ideas.title: /desktop doctor
ideas.pitch: One command that walks every layer between the palette and a visible window, and says which one is broken, with evidence.
ideas.experience: Nothing opens when you pick Firefox. You type /desktop doctor and a small checklist fills in line by line: catalog 214 apps, Ghostty Call gate present, agent answering, compositor up, test launch queued, panel id 7 mapped. The fourth line is red: the agent is running without --windows wayland, and the fix is printed beside it.
ideas.how: A DoctorService in XivDesktop.Plugin runs the checks in order off the framework thread: CatalogService snapshot count and scan time, IpcContract.GhosttyCall/GhosttyPost HasAction, agent.status and focus.get through GhosttyCallBackend, then an opt-in launch of a harmless app and a wait for its request id to resolve in window.list's requests. Each step is a pure record in Core (step, evidence, verdict, fix) so the reasoning is host-testable; the result renders in a small ImGui window and can be copied as a redacted report for the issue template the README asks for.
ideas.risks: It can only report what the IPC tells it; a mapped panel is still not proof the player can see it. The test launch starts a real program on the host, so it must be explicit and use something the player picks. The copied report must strip home paths, tokens and window titles.
ideas.audience: every new player setting it up, and whoever answers their issues

ideas.title: Open With, from inside the game
ideas.pitch: Pick a file in an in-game file dialog and open it in the right host app, using the %f and %u codes the Exec parser already knows about.
ideas.experience: You want the fight notes PDF beside you before a prog session. Palette, type 'open', choose the file from ~/Documents in a Dalamud file dialog, and the palette offers the three apps whose MimeType claims PDFs. A panel with the document lands at your shoulder.
ideas.how: ExecLine.StripFieldCodes currently expands %f %F %u %U to nothing; add a variant that substitutes one or many shell-quoted Linux paths. DesktopEntryParser keeps MimeType; AppCatalog builds a mime index. The picker is Dalamud's FileDialogManager over Z:\, and HostPaths maps the chosen Wine path back to the Linux path before it goes to window.open. A new PaletteCommand kind 'open' and a right-click 'Open file with…' in LauncherWindow.
ideas.risks: Mime detection needs a guess from the extension or the agent running xdg-mime; Wine cannot see everything the host can. Flatpak apps need their --file-forwarding markers kept rather than dropped. Paths with odd characters are exactly where quoting bugs hide, so this needs fuzz tests beside FuzzTests.
ideas.audience: raiders with notes and spreadsheets, writers, anyone who opens files more than apps

ideas.title: Right-Click Actions from the .desktop File
ideas.pitch: Show each app's own [Desktop Action] entries, such as a new private window or a compose message, as palette row actions.
ideas.experience: Highlight Firefox in the palette and the hint row reads Enter launch, Ctrl+P private window. Thunderbird offers Compose. It feels like the host's launcher, because it is reading the same file.
ideas.how: DesktopEntryParser ignores every group but [Desktop Entry]; parse the listed Actions groups into DesktopEntry.Actions (name, Exec, Icon) and run each Exec through ExecLine like the main one. PaletteEngine.RowActions appends them after the built-in actions; LauncherWindow's context menu lists them under Launch. AppSummary gains an optional actions list, an additive change to IpcContract.
ideas.risks: Chord assignment for arbitrary actions can collide with existing row keys, so only the first few get one. Some apps put odd things in actions that assume a running session bus.
ideas.audience: keyboard-first players, anyone used to a full desktop launcher

ideas.title: Real Icons, Not Letter Tiles
ideas.pitch: Have ghostty-agent rasterise SVG-only icons once on the host so the grid and taskbar stop falling back to letter tiles.
ideas.experience: Half your grid used to be coloured squares with a single letter. After one rescan, the Inkscape, GIMP and Steam icons are there at the grid's icon size, and they stay after a restart.
ideas.how: IconResolver already reports IconKind.SvgOnly. Collect those names after a scan and ask the agent for a PNG cache path per name at Configuration.IconSize (a new agent method, rendered with whatever the host has, such as rsvg); cache under XDG_CACHE_HOME keyed by source path and mtime, then map through HostPaths.ToLocal so ITextureProvider opens it. No new dependency in the plugin.
ideas.risks: Needs a ghostty-dalamud and agent change, so it only helps players on a matching build. Without the agent, letter tiles remain. Icon themes vary; the cache has to be invalidated when themes change.
ideas.audience: everyone who opens the app grid

ideas.title: Press the Chord to Bind It
ideas.pitch: Record a key chord by pressing it in Settings, and be told straight away if Wine never delivered it.
ideas.experience: Settings, Keybinds, click the terminal row and press Super+Enter. Nothing arrives: the row says 'no key seen in 3 seconds, your desktop may be taking Super'. You press Ctrl+Alt+Enter instead, it records, and a small warning notes the game's own binding for that chord.
ideas.how: KeybindService already reads IKeyState with a GetAsyncKeyState fallback; add a capture mode that suspends ChordTracker, waits for the first non-modifier key and builds a KeyChord from the held modifiers, then writes it to Configuration.Keybinds through the existing SettingsWindow Keybinds tab. The timeout message is the useful part: it is the first direct evidence of whether Wine passes the modifier at all.
ideas.risks: The game still acts on the keys while recording, so a chord bound to a game action fires once. Some compositors only drop Super on release. Cannot see what the game has bound without reading keybind data, so the conflict hint stays heuristic.
ideas.audience: everyone setting up keys, especially GNOME and KDE users whose desktop eats Super

ideas.title: Apps on Your Hotbar, by Macro
ideas.pitch: A palette action that copies a ready /desktop launch line for any app, so it can live in a user macro on your hotbar.
ideas.experience: Highlight Blender, press Ctrl+M, and the palette says 'copied /desktop launch org.blender.Blender'. Paste it into a User Macro, give it an icon, drag it to your crafting bar. Now the tool you plan melds in is one slot away.
ideas.how: PaletteCommand.Copy already exists and LauncherWindow already has 'Copy command'. Add a RowAction in PaletteEngine.RowActions that copies '/desktop launch <desktop-file id>'; the plugin's command handler already resolves ids first. The id is stable across rescans, unlike the name.
ideas.risks: XivDesktop does not write the macro itself; touching the game's macro data is out of bounds, so the player pastes by hand. Macros are shared per character and can be synced; an id for an app you later remove just fails with a message.

ideas.title: Controller Ring Launcher
ideas.pitch: A radial app ring on the gamepad for Steam Deck and couch players, with favourites on the sticks and workspaces on the shoulder buttons.
ideas.experience: On the Deck, hold a chosen button combo and your eight favourites fan out in a ring. Flick the stick toward the browser and release; the window lands as a pet. L1 and R1 step through workspaces while the ring is up.
ideas.how: Read IGamepadState in KeybindService alongside IKeyState and feed a pad chord into ChordTracker. The ring is a new ImGui window drawing UserLists favourites with IconDrawer; stick angle picks a sector. Launch and workspace steps go through CommandRunner, so nothing new reaches Ghostty.
ideas.risks: Any button combo the ring uses is also read by the game; it must be a chord the player chooses and ideally one the game leaves unbound. Panel apps still want a keyboard, so this launches and arranges, it does not make a browser controller-friendly.
ideas.audience: Steam Deck players, controller players, couch setups

ideas.title: Glamour Plates for Your Desk
ideas.pitch: Save a named set of apps and placements, and put the whole arrangement on with one palette entry.
ideas.experience: Type '>plate raid' and your prog layout goes on like a glamour: the spreadsheet docked left, the timeline tool as a pet, voice chat on workspace 2. '>plate cozy' swaps to a music player and a book for the inn room. Each plate shows its pieces before you apply it.
ideas.how: A Layout record in Core (app id, workspace, pin args, order) with a pure planner that diffs it against the current window list, the way WorkspaceModel.Plan already diffs visibility. Applying launches missing apps through window.open, waits for request ids to resolve in window.list's requests, then issues window.place and the workspace moves. Saved in Configuration beside Workspaces; exposed as palette rows and an additive XivDesktop.v1 gate.
ideas.risks: Windows appear asynchronously and some apps open several windows or a splash first, so matching window to app is fuzzy (WindowApps helps). Placement arguments are relative to the character, so the same plate lands differently in different spots. Launching six apps at once is slow.
ideas.audience: raiders, crafters, streamers, anyone with more than three regular apps

ideas.title: The Desk Knows Where You Are
ideas.pitch: Bind a layout or workspace to a territory, so your house, the inn and Limsa each get their own arrangement back when you arrive.
ideas.experience: You enter your apartment and the reading lamp app and the notes panel reappear where you left them by the window. Teleport to Ul'dah for the market and they fold away, leaving only the price sheet. Nothing moves in duties unless you said so.
ideas.how: Subscribe to IClientState.TerritoryChanged in SessionService (AskService already does). A small Core map from territory id, and for housing the ward and plot where the client state exposes it, to a plate name or workspace number. On change, run the same layout planner as named plates. The Configuration gains a per-territory table; ARCHITECTURE.md already lists this as planned.
ideas.risks: Zone changes happen while panels are mid-request; everything must wait until the load finishes. Housing identifiers are less stable than territory ids across patches. Instanced areas share a territory, so the match may be coarser than the player expects.
ideas.audience: housing enthusiasts, roleplayers, crafters and gatherers with a home base

ideas.title: Change Job, Change Desk
ideas.pitch: Link a gearset or job to a workspace, so switching to a crafter brings the crafting spreadsheet and switching to a tank brings the raid notes.
ideas.experience: You click your Carpenter gearset. As the gear swaps, workspace 3 slides in with the rotation sheet and the market board notes. Back to Warrior for roulettes, and it returns to the quiet workspace with only chat.
ideas.how: Poll the local player's ClassJob once per frame in the IFramework.Update tick KeybindService already runs, or on a class-change event where Dalamud offers one. A Configuration map from ClassJob row id to workspace number, applied through SessionService's existing workspace switch and WorkspaceModel.Plan. Only the player's own job is read.
ideas.risks: Fast gear swaps must be debounced. Switching workspace hides panels; a hidden video keeps playing sound, so this can surprise. Must never fire in a duty unless enabled separately.
ideas.audience: crafters and gatherers, job-hopping players, raiders

ideas.title: The Chocobo Saddlebag Scratchpad
ideas.pitch: A sway-style scratchpad: stow any panel out of sight with one chord and summon it back to your shoulder with another.
ideas.experience: The calculator app and a music player live in the saddlebag. Super+minus stows the focused panel. Super+grave brings the most recent one back as a pet beside you, and pressing it again cycles to the next thing in the bag.
ideas.how: Add a scratchpad as workspace 0 in WorkspaceModel (outside Count's 1-9), so Plan hides its panels regardless of the current workspace. Two new KeyAction entries in Core/Input/Keybinds.cs with defaults, handled in CommandRunner; summoning uses window.hide off plus window.toggle_pet or window.place with the configured PinArgs.
ideas.risks: Needs window.hide from the newer Ghostty methods; on older backends it falls back to minimise or is unavailable. Workspace persistence must not treat 0 as an orphan to clean up.
ideas.audience: sway and i3 users, anyone with small tools they check often

ideas.title: Proper Icons on the Umbra Taskbar
ideas.pitch: Show each open window's real app icon in the Umbra Windows widget instead of a letter tile.
ideas.experience: Your toolbar reads like a desktop panel: the browser globe, the terminal, the chat app, each with the workspace number beside it. The one that just opened has a thin highlight for a few seconds.
ideas.how: WindowsWidget.Item sets a LetterTile colour and letter today. Add an optional icon path to AppSummary and the Windows payload in IpcContract (additive, as the contract requires), filled from CatalogService's resolved PNG path, and let the widget load it through Una.Drawing's image style. Falls back to the letter tile when absent.
ideas.risks: The Umbra layout and the reflection-based popup workaround are themselves unverified in game. Icon textures must be loaded once and shared, not per redraw. Depends on desk-svg-icons for full coverage.

ideas.title: One Clipboard for Both Worlds
ideas.pitch: Copy in a host app panel and paste into game chat, or the other way round, through the agent.
ideas.experience: You copy a PF description out of the browser panel and paste it straight into the Party Finder comment box. Later you copy a player's macro text from chat and paste it into your notes app. No alt-tab, no second clipboard to think about.
ideas.how: The game side is Wine's Windows clipboard, reachable from the plugin through ImGui's clipboard functions. The compositor side needs ghostty-agent to act as a Wayland data-device client in its own compositor. XivDesktop would watch for a change on either side and relay text only, with a size cap, through a new agent method; PaletteCommand.Copy already writes the game side.
ideas.risks: Needs agent work in ghostty-dalamud. Password managers put secrets on the clipboard, so relaying must be opt-in, text only and skip sensitive MIME hints. Two-way sync loops need care. Wine's clipboard is already bridged to the host X11 or Wayland session on some setups, which could produce three clipboards fighting.
ideas.audience: everyone who uses a browser panel, raid leaders, crafters copying rotations

ideas.title: Moogle Delivery for App Notifications
ideas.pitch: Show notifications from apps running in the compositor as Dalamud toasts, with the app's icon and a click that focuses its panel.
ideas.experience: Mid-roulette, a small toast slides in: your chat app, one new message from your partner. You finish the pull, click the toast, and the chat panel comes forward on its workspace.
ideas.how: The agent owns org.freedesktop.Notifications on the session bus it gives its compositor's apps and forwards summary, body and app id as a new event in window.list or a separate method. SessionService already raises Dalamud notifications through INotificationManager for panel open and end; extend Notify with the app's icon from CatalogService and a click that runs PaletteCommand.Focus.
ideas.risks: Depends entirely on agent changes and on apps using the session bus the agent controls. Notification bodies are private and would show on stream; needs a 'title only' option. Rate limiting is needed for chatty apps.
ideas.audience: everyone who keeps chat or mail apps in a panel

ideas.title: Let XivMcp Drive the Desk
ideas.pitch: Ship the planned list_apps, launch_app, list_windows, window_action, switch_workspace and palette_search tools in XivMcp, on top of the XivDesktop.v1 gates that already exist.
ideas.experience: You ask your local model to 'set me up for the savage prog'. It lists your apps, opens the timeline sheet and the recording tool, puts them on workspace 2 and tells you which ones it could not find, all through tools you can see and approve.
ideas.how: The gates are in src/Shared/IpcContract.cs (ListApps, Launch, Windows, Workspace, Palette, WindowAction) with parse helpers already. XivMcp registers thin tools that call them and return the JSON as is. Launch returns queued, not done, so launch_app should poll Windows for the new panel before reporting success.
ideas.risks: A model that can launch apps can run programs on the host; launch_app needs a per-call confirmation or an allow list, the way the Claude permission dialog works. Tool results must say 'queued' honestly rather than 'opened'. Lives mostly in another repository.
ideas.audience: Almanac and Claude users, automation-minded players

ideas.title: Send This Window to Eorzea
ideas.pitch: A GNOME Shell entry that hands a window already running on your desktop to the game as a panel.
ideas.experience: You are reading a guide in the host browser, then launch the game. From the browser's window menu you choose Send to game, and a moment later that same page is floating as a pet beside your character, still scrolled to the same place.
ideas.how: Moving an already-mapped window into the agent's compositor is not possible as such; GUIDE.md's planned route is the agent capturing it through the desktop portal's screencast, as it does on Windows. A small Shell extension calls the agent (not Wine) with the window's identity; the agent starts a capture and the game gets a window.open with a match. XivDesktop's part is palette and taskbar support for captured panels.
ideas.risks: A captured window is a picture plus forwarded input, not a native panel; input forwarding through the portal is limited. The portal prompts the user every time on many setups. GNOME extension APIs change every release. Nothing of this exists yet.
ideas.audience: GNOME users, people who run the game as one part of their desktop

ideas.title: Stow the Desk When the Duty Pops
ideas.pitch: When you enter a duty or combat starts, hide every window panel, and put them back exactly as they were when it ends.
ideas.experience: The queue pops while you are reading a wiki panel. You commence, and the panels fold away before the first loading screen. After the last boss, as the chest appears, they return to the same workspace and positions.
ideas.how: Plugin.cs already receives ICondition (AskService uses it). A DutyGuard in SessionService watches BoundByDuty and InCombat with a short settle delay, remembers WorkspaceModel's state, and hides everything through the same Plan and window.hide path workspaces use; the exit restores it. Per-condition toggles in Settings, General, plus an exception list for apps the player wants kept, such as voice chat.
ideas.risks: Hiding is presentation only: a video keeps playing and audio keeps going. If a panel owns the keyboard when a pull starts, focus must return to the game first or it is dangerous. Condition flags flicker around cutscenes and zoning, so a naive watcher will thrash.
ideas.audience: everyone who queues with panels open, healers especially

ideas.title: The Veil
ideas.pitch: One chord, or GPose starting, hides private panels and blanks window titles in the palette, taskbar and notifications.
ideas.experience: You enter GPose for a party photo. Your mail and chat panels disappear, the Umbra taskbar reads 'Window, Window, Window', and the open and close toasts stop naming apps. Leave GPose and it lifts.
ideas.how: A Veiled flag in SessionService, set by a new KeyAction and by IClientState's GPose state. When set, PaletteEngine gets a context with titles masked, the Windows gate returns masked titles to the Umbra widget, SessionService.Notify drops names, and panels tagged private in Configuration are hidden through window.hide.
ideas.risks: XivDesktop cannot mask the contents of a panel it hides late: anything captured in the first frame is already out. Other plugins drawing window titles are not covered. It must be clear this reduces exposure, not a guarantee.
ideas.audience: GPose photographers, streamers, anyone sharing screenshots
